content:
incbot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT: GPU pool 'prefill' at 98% utilization for 12m, queue depth growing — autoscaler hit hard limit. Severity: P1. Affected routes: /api/v1/generate (hosted). Paging oncall.

maria: oncall here. seeing massive queue growth on prefill-prefetchers. dashboards show sustained KV cache fills and prefill rate spiking after the v21.4 model patch.

raj: I just noticed the new tokenizer/model change increased average context by ~40% for warmup requests. KV entries are much larger, prefill tasks take longer -> concurrent slots occupied.

lee: autoscaler events show repeated scale attempts: desired replicas jumped but hit max_replicas=48. Pool CPU/GPU quotas exhausted in eu-west-1. Logs show throttles at the request router level.

ash: vendor capacity pool also responded slowly; provisioning request latency > 30s so scale up didn't catch up. We're at the point where queueing makes tail latencies explode and more prefill tasks are spawned -> feedback.

julia: Support: multiple customers reporting 500s and increase in request timeouts. CS is triaging high-value customers; some are on Dedicated though. We need an external comms status ASAP.

maria: immediate mitigation plan: 1) stop rollout (rollback) 2) throttle prefill/warmup rate globally 3) bump autoscaler soft limit if cloud allows 4) divert some traffic to older model variant. Who can cut the canary and roll back? @raj

raj: I'm rolling back the v21.4 canary now — stopping the deployment and pinning traffic to v21.3 for hosted. Doing a quick patch to disable the new prefetcher flag.

devops-bot: deployment/v21.4 -> rollback initiated by raj at 3305123468. Canary termination in progress.

lee: while rollback happens, set a temporary circuit on prefill routes: set rate-limit 10r/s per pool and set prefill_max_concurrency=2 in routing config to slow warmups.

ash: I'll push the routing change to limit prefill concurrency across eu-west-1 and us-west-2. Patch coming: /deployments/routing/prefill-rate-limit.

maria: also please disable 'eager-kv-prefetch' feature flag for hosted (ff:eager_kv_prefetch=false). That should reduce KV churn.

raj: Flag disabled. Confirmed off in config service. v21.4 rollback completed and traffic shifted to v21.3 — canary repointed to stable. Monitoring for queue drop.

lee: Autoscaler logs — we hit policy hard_limit=48 but cloud quota is 48 GPUs. I filed a quota increase request but that will take hours. In the short term, we need to reduce load.

devops-bot: routing change applied by ash at 3305123505: prefill_rate_limit=10r/s, prefill_max_concurrency=2.

maria: early signs: queue depth dropping from 5600 -> 1800 in 3m. CPU on prefill workers down 35%. Latency tail reducing but still elevated.

julia: CS updated customers with interim note: "We are rolling back a recent model update and applying temporary throttles to restore service stability. We will follow up with a root cause and timeline within 2 hours." Some customers asking for ETA on rollback verification.

raj: Observed an interesting pattern in logs: certain client prefixes trigger larger prefill contexts (multi-turn system prompts). Need to add a quick mitigation to cap client prefill tokens to 1024 for hosted plans.

ash: Implemented soft cap at ingress: prefill_token_cap=1024 for hosted API. Clients receiving larger requests will get 429 for prefill but main inference path still allowed.

lee: Good move. That reduces KV size per session and prevents runaway slots. Queue now 400 and falling.

maria: Assessing customer impact: approx 7% of requests experienced timeouts during peak window (3305123440 - 3305123500). High-value customers were routed to older model and some experienced degraded perf but no data loss.

julia: Logged impacted customer list; CS owners assigned. We'll open a post-incident call after stabilization.

raj: Follow-ups we need: a) add automatic prefill rate-limiter tied to autoscaler headroom b) add safety to not allow model changes that increase average context by >20% without rollout gating c) revisit max_replicas/quota contract with cloud vendor.

maria: I'll create incident ticket and schedule an RCA. For now we'll keep the throttle in place for 1 hour, then gradually remove if stable. Handing back to oncall monitoring. If queue <100 and error rate <1% for 15m we close.

lee: Agreed — handing off monitoring to eng-sre rotation. I'm staying available for 30m. Marking mitigation: rollback + prefill caps + routing throttles.

devops-bot: NOTE: Incident resolved? status_hint=stabilizing. last_metric_drop at 3305123590. Please update severity if needed.

maria: moving to monitoring. severity -> P2 (impact reduced). Will update the incident doc with timestamps and mitigation steps.

julia: CS updated customers with final note and interim workaround suggestions. No major escalations outstanding.

raj: I'll prepare a quick changelist to prevent similar regressions: add rollout perf test that simulates KV-warmup and checks autoscaler headroom. Opening PR now.

maria: thanks everyone. handing to eng-sre for postmortem capture. If anything regresses ping me directly.

lee: handback acknowledged. I'll kick off the incident writeup and tag relevant teams. Closing thread when RCA doc ready.
